vocabulary.meaning_en: the relationship a company has with its customers
vocabulary.example: Good customer relations bring repeat business.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to keep something in good condition or at the same level
vocabulary.example: We must maintain good relations with our clients.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person or company that pays for a service or product
vocabulary.example: Our client in France is happy with the order.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the help a company gives its customers
vocabulary.example: It's good customer service to call them.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not having the skill to do a job well
vocabulary.example: The project failed because of incompetence.

vocabulary.meaning_en: annoyed because you can't do or change something
vocabulary.example: I feel frustrated when my work is wasted.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to fix a confusing or bad situation
vocabulary.example: I need to call the client and sort out the mess.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say that you no longer want goods you ordered
vocabulary.example: I called the supplier and cancelled the order.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the documents connected with a job or order
vocabulary.example: Here's the paperwork for the order.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to solve a problem and stop a bad situation
vocabulary.example: Tom saved the day by sending the right order.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to get involved in something that is not your business
vocabulary.example: I don't want to interfere, but have you called them?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to get something that is sent to you
vocabulary.note_ar: قاعدة: i قبل e إلا بعد c.
vocabulary.note_en: Spelling rule: i before e except after c.
vocabulary.example: Did you receive our order?

vocabulary.meaning_en: happy with something
vocabulary.example: We hope you are pleased with our service.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the work a company does for its customers
vocabulary.example: Thank you for using our service.

vocabulary.meaning_en: choose our company again in the future
vocabulary.example: We hope you will use us again.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to tell someone your name and where you are from
vocabulary.example: Always introduce yourself at the start of a call.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a call to check that everything is fine after a sale
vocabulary.example: I'll make a follow-up call next week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to deal with something that needs doing
vocabulary.example: There is still some business to attend to.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to create problems
vocabulary.example: She's causing so much trouble.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to spoil or damage a situation
vocabulary.example: Rachel has messed things up again.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a situation that needs you to do something
vocabulary.example: This calls for action.

fine_lines.title: client vs customer
fine_lines.explanation_ar: customer هو من يشتري منتجًا من متجر أو شركة، وغالبًا تكون العلاقة قصيرة. client يُستخدم غالبًا لمن يتلقى خدمة مهنية أو يتعامل مع الشركة بشكل منتظم (مثل الشركات والمحامين).
fine_lines.explanation_en: A customer buys goods from a shop or company. A client usually receives a professional service or has a regular business relationship with a company.

examples.sentence: The shop was full of customers.
We called our client in France.

fine_lines.title: pleased with vs pleased to
fine_lines.explanation_ar: pleased with + اسم: راضٍ عن شيء (pleased with our service). pleased to + فعل: سعيد بفعل شيء (pleased to meet you).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Pleased with + noun = happy with something. Pleased to + verb = happy to do something.

examples.sentence: We hope you are pleased with our service.

expressions.phrase: Hello, I'm Anna from Tip Top Trading. How are you today?
expressions.meaning_ar: مرحبًا، أنا آنا من شركة تيب توب تريدنغ. كيف حالك اليوم؟
expressions.meaning_en: A friendly way to start a call to a client.
expressions.example: Hello, I'm Sara from Green Office Supplies. How are you today?

expressions.phrase: I hope you have received our order and are happy with it.
expressions.meaning_ar: آمل أن تكونوا قد استلمتم طلبكم وأنكم راضون عنه.
expressions.meaning_en: Checking that the client got the goods.
expressions.example: I hope you have received our order and are happy with it.

expressions.phrase: We do hope you are pleased with our service and that you may use us again.
expressions.meaning_ar: نأمل حقًا أن تكونوا راضين عن خدمتنا وأن تتعاملوا معنا مجددًا.
expressions.example: We do hope you are pleased with our service and that you may use us again.

expressions.phrase: Do you have any questions you may want to ask?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل لديكم أي أسئلة تودّون طرحها؟
expressions.meaning_en: Inviting the client to ask questions.
expressions.example: Before I go, do you have any questions you may want to ask?

expressions.meaning_en: Thanking someone who solved a problem.
expressions.example: Thanks for fixing the printer – you saved the day!

expressions.phrase: I don't want to interfere, but…
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to give advice.
expressions.example: I don't want to interfere, but have you called the client?
Three complaints in one day? This calls for action.

grammar.title: Emphatic do: We do hope…
grammar.explanation_ar: نضيف do/does قبل الفعل في الجملة المثبتة لتأكيد المعنى وإظهار الصدق: We do hope you are pleased. وهي شائعة في اللغة الرسمية المهذبة.
grammar.explanation_en: Add do/does before the verb in a positive sentence to make it stronger and more sincere: We do hope you are pleased. It is common in polite, formal English.
examples: We do hope you are pleased with our service.

grammar.title: may for polite possibility
grammar.explanation_ar: تُستخدم may بمعنى (قد / ربما) بأسلوب مهذب ورسمي: that you may use us again و questions you may want to ask.
grammar.explanation_en: 'may' shows possibility in a polite, formal way: that you may use us again; questions you may want to ask.
examples: We hope you may use us again.
Do you have any questions you may want to ask?

grammar.title: I hope + present perfect
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد I hope نستخدم المضارع التام للحديث عن شيء يُفترض أنه حدث: I hope you have received our order.
grammar.explanation_en: After 'I hope' use the present perfect to talk about something that should have happened: I hope you have received our order.
examples: I hope you have received our order.
I hope you have had a good trip.
I hope the parcel has arrived safely.

questions.question: How should Anna start the call to her client?
choices: Hello, I'm Anna from Tip Top Trading. How are you today?
questions.explanation_ar: البداية المهذبة: التعريف بالنفس والسؤال عن الحال.
questions.explanation_en: A polite start: say who you are and ask how they are.

questions.question: Complete: 'We ___ hope you are pleased with our service.'
Complete: 'I hope you have ___ our order.'
What does 'save the day' mean?
choices: solve a problem and stop a bad situation
questions.explanation_ar: save the day تعني إنقاذ الموقف.
questions.explanation_en: It means solving a problem at the last moment.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: We hope you are pleasing with our service.
We hope you are pleased to our service.
We hope you are pleased with our service.
We hope you please with our service.

questions.question: Which word means 'a person or company that pays for a professional service'?
questions.explanation_en: A client pays for a service.

questions.question: 'Do you have any questions you ___ want to ask?'
questions.explanation_ar: may هنا للتعبير المهذب عن الاحتمال.
questions.explanation_en: 'may' is the polite word used here.

questions.question: Tom says: 'I don't want to interfere, but…' What is he doing?
questions.explanation_en: It's a polite way to start giving advice.

questions.question: What is 'paperwork'?
choices: documents connected with an order or job
questions.explanation_en: Paperwork is the documents for a job.

questions.question: 'Rachel has messed things up again' means…
choices: she has made a good deal
she has spoiled the situation again
questions.explanation_ar: mess things up تعني إفساد الأمور.
questions.explanation_en: Mess things up means spoil the situation.
